open_points.subject: Negative derived allocation totals
open_points.text: “with one named exception: an expense allocation amount (M26, M29); otherwise negative values exist only in derived balances” conflicts with M26’s “zero and negative amounts are accepted and stored” because derived `material_actual`, `material_actual_total`, or `other_expenses_total` can then be negative even though they are not balances.
open_points.question: May exact aggregation of accepted negative allocations produce negative actual-material or Other-expenses values, and if so are those values additional permitted negative derived facts despite not being balances?
options: Expose the exact negative derived totals.
Constrain accepted allocation sets so non-balance derived totals cannot become negative.
Apply some special treatment when deriving those totals.
open_points.default_guess: Expose the exact negative derived totals because the allocations are explicitly accepted and derived values are required to remain deterministic and unclamped.

witness.initial: An active project has a manual budget with section A and no existing expenses.
events: An operator creates a EUR 100 expense with allocations of EUR -20 to section A and EUR 120 to Other expenses.
A viewer reads the project budget and expense summary.
outcomes: The intake succeeds and the viewer sees section A material actual of EUR -20 and Other expenses of EUR 120, treating the allocation exception as permitting its exact derived consequences.
The implementation refuses the allocation or cannot expose the negative section actual because the modeling convention permits negative derived values only for balances.
witness.observer: The operator sees whether intake succeeds, and the viewer sees whether the exact negative actual is readable.
